messages:
maya: Quick sync — drafting PRD for Dedicated Capacity SLA + autoscale. Need to lock acceptance criteria today.
liam: +1. I pushed a PR with initial numbers: https://git.internal/r/redwood/prs/2345. Key question: p99 target 350ms vs 500ms for bursty workloads?
sophia: FYI SRE perspective: autoscale cooldown 60s causes overshoot on short bursts. Suggest 30s with rate-limited scale-up (cap 2x/min).
liam: 30s scale-up ok, but noisy scaler risk. Propose: immediate hot-pool up to a burst buffer (20% of reserved), then gradual scale to requested capacity.
zhen: From SE: need per-customer hard queues to avoid noisy neighbors. We should document shed policy: prefer 429 + retry-after for short queues, otherwise queued with fair-share.
omar: Customer asks to guarantee no 5xx on fallback. How does canary fallback to hosted model work in practice?
liam: Fallback flow: node failure or full queue -> route to hosted model variant with token cap and degraded latency SLA. Must emit billing/cost warning and notify customer via webhook.
maya: Draft acceptance criteria below — please comment inline:
- p99 <= 350ms at reserved throughput for 95% of 24h windows
- During autoscale ramp, p99 <= 500ms for up to 10 minutes
- Autoscale should achieve 2x baseline sustained capacity within 90s for load > 2 minutes
- Burst buffer must absorb spikes <=15s without triggering full scale-out
- KV cache warmup <= 60s for hot prefixes (measured median)
- Error rate (5xx) <= 1% weekly; any spike >3x baseline triggers auto-canary rollback
- Canary rollback automated when error_rate_5m > 3x baseline AND p50_latency > 2x baseline for 10m
- Rollout playbook + oncall runbook documented in PRD
sophia: Health signals to drive autoscale and rollback: queue_depth, avg_latency_30s, error_rate_5m, cpu_util, kv_cache_miss_rate. Rollback signal = error_rate_5m > 3x baseline AND p50_latency > 2x baseline.
liam: Edge cases we need spelled out in PRD: short intense spikes (<=15s) should not trigger full scale. Long noisy spikes require vertical scale + admission control. Also define behavior for partial GPU failures.
zhen: Edge: cold-start for large models (RLHF) can blow kv cache and cause long tails. Add option in PRD for "pre-warm window" and a warm-pool of standby replicas.
maya: Test plan (high level): load tests with synthetic traffic profiles: sustained baseline, 5% bursts at 10x for 10s, 1% bursts at 10x for 60s. Add chaos tests for partial node loss and simulated KV cache eviction.
omar: I'll get customer sign-off on fallback language and SLA credits formula. They want explicit credit calc for degraded fallback vs full outage.
deploy-bot: deploy started: prd/sla-dedicated/latest at 1881234890 :rocket:
liam: Nice. Next steps: formalize acceptance criteria into the PRD markdown, add a short cutover runbook for oncall, and include load test harness links.
maya: I'll update PRD and ping for final review before EOD. Thanks all :pray:
